vocabulary.normalization_policy: Unicode NFKC; casefold; fold dotted or spaced initialisms (R.D.L., R D L, rdl); remove apostrophes; convert other punctuation to spaces; collapse whitespace. Resolver priority: canonical, exercise alias, explicit ambiguity, family registry, unknown. No fuzzy override of explicit equipment, position, angle, grip, assistance, or laterality.
vocabulary.workout_role_policy: Warm-up, working set, and cooldown are workout/session context, not exercise identities.
vocabulary.unmatched_input_policy: Unknown inputs remain valid user free text; no forced match.
vocabulary.specificity_policy: Unmodified common names may identify the established base exercise (e.g. burpees, situp, leg press, lat pulldown). Terms omitting material equipment or technique distinctions otherwise remain family_only or ambiguous. Weighted, assisted, unilateral, stance, and grip variants retain separate IDs.

validation_summary.equipment_count_definition: Number of exercise entries requiring each equipment type. One exercise may count in multiple equipment categories.

manual_model_review.scope: Targeted model/semantic inspection of weighted loading implements, machine-versus-band assistance, bar placement and treadmill grade. No systematic external biomechanical audit.

limitations: Machine setup, attachment, resistance path, and body position can vary by manufacturer; no universal machine equivalence is asserted.
An unspecified-grip/base record is not identical to an explicitly named grip or stance variant for purposes of merging existing histories.
Some generic colloquialisms have different gym-specific meanings. Ambiguous or unsupported user inputs must stay editable free text.
Rotator cuff muscles are distinguished for shoulder rotation, but other exercise muscle classifications still reflect broad targets rather than measured muscle contribution.
Aliases and heuristic qualifiers are curated, not a promise of exhaustive semantic/biomechanical validation.
